scope: LeaChat runtime-status observation UI. The live API was read once and the live database was inspected read-only; tests use HTTP/browser fixtures. No commands, compiler checks or provider calls were started.
diagnosis: All unsuccessful runtime-status HTTP responses and transport exceptions became state=unavailable without distinguishing missing SQL observations from checker health.
Unavailable status was not eligible for polling when the selected session was idle, so a transient error could remain visible after recovery.
The inspected current response contains no runtime failure. The exact earlier browser HTTP failure is not retained in this evidence; it is not established as a compiler failure.
fix: Retain the distinction between projection_unavailable (waiting for status), status API/network failure (reconnecting), and a successful unavailable runtime report (existing runtime warning).
Re-read unavailable observations every five seconds while visible, including idle sessions; retain abort, session-switch and visibility guards.
Show pending observations in neutral styling and preserve server explanations in the tooltip without writing them as compiler failures.
Continue using only the SQL-backed GET status endpoint; no direct Lean/LSP or worker calls.

browser_scenarios: Initial SQL observation unavailable, then healthy idle response with no active run.
Initial network failure, then healthy idle response.
Successful API response reporting genuine unavailable state, then healthy idle response.
browser_observations: All three cases retry and clear the chip after recovery.
Draft content, focus and selection remain unchanged.
Pending-state desktop and narrow renders were reviewed.
